record_type_quote: Push button reproduction attempt of a research claim from Woltin et al. (2011)

targets.authors: Woltin, K.-A., Corneille, O., Yzerbyt, V. Y., & Förster, J.
targets.title: Narrowing down to open up for other people's concerns: Empathic concern can be enhanced by inducing detailed processing.
targets.evidence_quote: We selected the claim that the detailed, concrete processing style associated with low power should facilitate empathic concern (Statement 2), which reflects "In three experiments inducing a detailed versus abstract processing style using perceptual (Experiment 1), motivational (Experiment 2), and social (Experiment 3) manipulations, we found that empathic concerns are enhanced in contexts associated with a more detailed processing style (i.e., local perceptual scope, prevention motivation, and low power, respectively)" (Statement 1), as found in the paper's abstract. The claim is tested by an ANOVA test using the power priming condition (low/high power) as the independent variable and empathic concern as the dependent variable (Statement 3), which resulted in power priming influencing participants' empathic concern, F(1,34) = 5.76, p = .022, partial eta squared = .15 - participants reported greater empathic concern when primed with low power (Statement 4).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: Confirmed. Greater empathic concern was reported when participants were primed with low compared to high power, F(1,34) = 5.758, p = .022, partial eta-squared = .145.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: To reproduce the focal test, the analyst needs both the POWER MAST MANI and PT EC RECODED data.sav datafile and Syntax.sps syntax file.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The same ANOVA produced matching F and p, with negligible rounding of partial eta squared. This push-button report uses the provided syntax to reproduce the focal test and describes no alternative specifications.
